clubs.name: Astrophysics Club
clubs.purpose: We're a student-led club that explores modern astrophysics and cosmology beyond what our regular science classes cover. At our meetings, we run student-led presentations and open discussions on topics like black hole physics, inflationary and pre-Big Bang cosmology, general relativity, and the black hole information paradox. Beyond our regular meetings, we bring in guest speakers, professors, graduate students, and researchers from universities and national labs, to share their work and give our members a real look at what modern astrophysics research looks like. We also connect members with outside opportunities like summer programs, competitions, and research experiences. Our goal is to build a community of curious students, make research-level ideas approachable, and give everyone a path into physics and astronomy beyond the classroom.

clubs.name: Developer Club
clubs.purpose: The Fremont Developer Club exists as a place for individuals interested in software development to share their interests, learn, and build real projects. We believe that all students should learn not only how to code, but how to apply that coding knowledge to build actual projects to showcase and learn from. We also want to give students the ability to actually choose their interests, and build projects that they actually want to build. We will adapt with them. As a club, we exist to bridge the gap between theoretical knowledge and practical execution, providing every student with the mentorship, tools, and collaboration necessary to turn creative ideas into functional applications. Furthermore, Developer Club provides the opportunity to showcase the members' skill in our annual hackathon, where we allow other schools across the Bay Area to compete and win prizes.

clubs.name: National Honor Society
clubs.purpose: The purpose of the National Honor Society (NHS) chapter is to recognize and honor outstanding high school students who have demonstrated excellence in scholarship, leadership, service, and character. Beyond mere recognition, our chapter aims to cultivate a culture of service and leadership development among its members. Through various activities and initiatives, we seek to not only celebrate academic achievement but also to instill in our members a sense of responsibility towards their community and a commitment to making a positive impact in the world.

clubs.name: National Personal Finance Challenge Club
clubs.purpose: The National Personal Finance Challenge Club prepares students for the National Personal Finance Challenge by building mastery of core personal finance topics, including budgeting, saving, credit management, risk management, investing, and income planning. Members organize into teams and practice analyzing real-life financial scenarios, making quick decisions under timed conditions to develop both financial literacy and strategic thinking. Beyond competition prep, the club aims to give students practical money-management skills they can apply to real-world financial decisions throughout their lives.

clubs.name: Neuroscience Club
clubs.purpose: The Neuroscience Club at Fremont High School inspires, educates, and welcomes students who want to learn about neuroscience. The objectives of this club are to bring awareness about the field of neuroscience to the school and youth, to learn how to analyze neuroscience-based scientific literature, to understand how mental health correlates to neuroscience, and to research the differences in the brain for different types of people. The club will also explore the human brain's evolution based on cultures, demographics, and environments. AI will also be used to gain a deeper understanding of the human brain and the field of neuroscience. With various discussions and projects, students will gain a greater appreciation for how the brain works and learn how fascinating our brains are.

This club encourages and provides students a place to contribute in helping adolescents around the world struggling with malnutrition, lack of safe shelter, natural conflicts, etc. UNICEF will host fundraisers, community service events, campaigns, other special events, and more along the way where members can make a positive impact while simultaneously gaining volunteer hours. clubs.name: Vet Connect
clubs.purpose: FHS Vet Connect is dedicated to closing the gap between students and the veterinary world through hands-on experience and networking. Our objective is to operate as a club at school focusing on animal advocacy and education. Outside of school, the club will produce podcasts and interviews with professionals including vets, vet techs, shelter workers, and more to discuss critical topics like mental health, school requirements, and career burnout. Additionally, we will partner with local institutions such as the SPCA, Animal Assisted Happiness, and Happy Hollow to provide members with various volunteer opportunities.
